He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He was selected in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the 56th pick before being traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. He played a season in the [[NBA G League]] with Brooklyn's affiliate, the [[Long Island Nets]] before beginning his European career in 2021. As a high school senior in 2017, he was selected to play in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]],{{Cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |date=February 7, 2017 |title=UCLA signee Jaylen Hands receives McDonald's All American jersey |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/ucla-signee-jaylen-hands-receives-mcdonalds-all-american-jersey |access-date=June 12, 2023 |website=usatodayhss.com}} and was ranked as a consensus five-star prospect and the No. 3 [[point guard]] in the country in the class of 2017 by all major scouting services, including [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports]]. Hands earned second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors in his sophomore year with UCLA in 2019. ==High school career== Hands began his high school career playing with [[Mater Dei Catholic High School (Chula Vista, California)|Mater Dei Catholic High School]] in [[Chula Vista, California]] where he was named an All-County player, San Diego Metro League Player of the Year, and won the 2014 [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] championship.{{Cite web |last=Maffei |first=John |date=September 21, 2015 |title=Hands makes two major decisions |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-jaylen-hands-balboa-city-ucla-2015sep21-story.html |access-date=June 12, 2023 |website=sandiegouniontribune.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/h/hands-jaylen.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907032712/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/h/hands-jaylen.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 7, 2015|title = Jaylen Hands}} Following his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Foothills Christian High School]] in [[El Cajon]], but this transfer was denied by the [[CIF San Diego Section|San Diego Section]]. Instead, Hands enrolled at Balboa City, a prep school that operated outside of the Section's jurisdiction, where he was teammates with [[Deandre Ayton]], the future top prospect of the class of 2017. For his senior season, he completed his transfer to Foothills Christian, where he played for coach [[Brad Leaf]], father of UCLA star [[T. J. Leaf]]. That year, Hands averaged 29 points, 6.7 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 6.5 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] a game.{{Cite web |last=Maffei |first=John |date=December 25, 2016 |title=Another After playing 14 games as a reserve with coach [[Steve Alford]] staggering the minutes of his two main ballhandlers, Hands returned to the starting lineup on January 25, 2018, against [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], replacing forward [[GG Goloman]].{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Thi|title=UCLA basketball beats Cal to snap 3-game losing streak|date=January 25, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2018/01/25/ucla-basketball-beats-cal-to-snap-3-game-losing-streak/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128183619/https://www.dailynews.com/2018/01/25/ucla-basketball-beats-cal-to-snap-3-game-losing-streak/|archive-date=January 28, 2018|url-status=live}} He finished with 14 points, six rebounds and one assist in a 70–57 win over the Golden Bears.{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|title=Jaylen Hands' return to the UCLA starting lineup may be just a cameo|date=January 26, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20180126-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128095827/http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-20180126-story.html|archive-date=January 28, 2018|url-status=live}} In the following game, he scored nine points and had a season-high 10 assists with only one turnover in an 89–73 victory over [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Thi|title=UCLA men's basketball makes it look easy in win over Stanford|date=January 27, 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2018/01/27/ucla-mens-basketball-makes-it-look-easy-in-win-over-stanford/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128171452/https://www.ocregister.com/2018/01/27/ucla-mens-basketball-makes-it-look-easy-in-win-over-stanford/|archive-date=January 28, 2018|url-status=live}} Hands missed the regular season finale after spraining his right ankle in practice. In [[2018–19 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2018–19]], Hands assumed the lead point guard role with Holiday having left for the [[NBA]]. Hands hoped to become a better leader and improve his assist-to-turnover ratio. He and fellow sophomore [[Kris Wilkes]] were the team's top two returning scorers.
